title: A debug heap of your own
hints: Keep a record per block: the raw pointer from `malloc`, the size the caller asked for, its number, and whether it has been released. The user pointer is `raw + GUARD_BYTES`, so finding a block from a user pointer is a search for `raw + GUARD_BYTES == p`.
Do not `free` on release: mark the block as freed, fill it with 0xDD and keep it. Only the destructor calls `std::free`, for every block. That quarantine is what makes writes after free detectable.
requirements: New blocks are filled with 0xCD and surrounded by 0xFD guards.
Overruns, underruns, double frees, invalid frees and writes after free are each reported with the right allocation number.
Freed blocks are kept in quarantine and filled with 0xDD.
Leaks and bytes in use are reported, and the heap releases all its memory when destroyed.
stretch: Record a short "where" string with each allocation (as `_CRTDBG_MAP_ALLOC` records the file and line) and print a leak report in the same format as the real debug heap, then feed it to your parser from lesson 4.05.
